title: Stabilize button layout and visual parity for icon-only + loading states across themes
creator: Anika Shah
description:
Problem: Several regressions landed after token consolidation and recent theming work where icon-only buttons show a horizontal/vertical jump when switching to loading or disabled. In some themes the spinner is misaligned and pushes neighboring content. This is most visible in compact layouts (table rows, dense toolbars) and on variant combinations (ghost + accent). The issue appears caused by inconsistent reserved space for the spinner, token mismatch for icon padding across sizes, and a missing baseline for icon/button intrinsic width in certain themes.

Why this matters: Layout shift creates a jarring UX during network or state transitions, increases perceived latency, and can cause mis-clicks. These controls are used in high-frequency places (row actions, repeating toolbars) so even small regressions amplify. We need a design spec and rollout that eliminates jumps, preserves visual parity across themes, and is accessible to assistive tech and reduced-motion users.
acceptance_criteria: Icon-only buttons do not change in overall width/height when swapping between default, loading, and disabled states (no layout shift in a standard toolbar at 320px+ widths)
Spinner occupies a reserved visual slot; content does not reflow during spinner start/stop in all official themes (light, dark, high-contrast)
Accessibility: buttons maintain correct aria-labels during loading (e.g., aria-busy or visually-hidden label) and pass keyboard focus visual checks
Design sign-off from Design Lead and Engineering (component owner) on the visual spec and interaction guidelines
Unit snapshots and integration storybook examples added for variants: icon-only small/medium/large + ghost/primary/secondary in light and dark themes
QA: e2e checks on toolbar + table rows that assert no layout shift when toggling loading state
design_notes: Root cause summary from triage: token consolidation changed left/right token values for icon padding in compact size and unintentionally switched spinner baseline from overlay to inline placement in the ghost variant. Some themes apply a subtle border in the compact token set which combined with spinner width produced a 2px width change that cascaded in dense layouts. We want to standardize a 'spinner slot' and formalize token names: button.icon.padding-inline, button.icon.spinner-slot-width, button.icon.fixed-diameter, and ensure theme overrides only modify color/contrast, not layout tokens.
proposed_solutions: Reserve spinner slot: always reserve a fixed-width slot (spinner-slot-width) in icon-only buttons and center spinner inside it; when not loading show a visually-hidden placeholder to preserve width
Token normalization: introduce explicit tokens for icon-only dimensions (icon-button-size-compact, icon-button-inner-gap) and update theme mappings to avoid per-theme layout overrides

CSS implementation: use flex container with min-width and min-height for button content; toggle visibility of spinner vs placeholder using opacity/visibility rather than changing layout; prefer transform-based motion for spinner rotation
Edge-case theme fix: remove border-width changes for compact ghost variant or account for them in the reserved slot calculation
Fallbacks: for third-party embeds or non-standard CSS envs, add an opt-in data attribute data-preserve-spinner to force slot behavior
accessibility_considerations: When in loading state, provide aria-busy=true on the button and update accessible name if status matters (e.g., 'Saving...' vs 'Save')
Ensure spinner is decorative if the label already communicates action; otherwise expose a succinct live region message under 250ms debounce
Respect prefers-reduced-motion: pause spinner animation and use subtle opacity change instead
Maintain focus ring visibility and keyboard operability when spinner overlays the button content
implementation_notes: Engineering PR: add reserved slot with .btn__spinner-slot element; ensure snapshot tests cover 'placeholder' state
Tokens: update token mapping sheet and send PR to tokens repo; create migration note for theming teams
Storybook: add stories for dense toolbar/table row combos and visual-diff baseline images
Metrics: instrument Lighthouse visual stability (Cumulative Layout Shift) on small set of pages pre/post rollout
qa_checklist: Manual test: Add icon-only buttons inside Table row actions; toggle loading 10x and observe no layout jump
Visual regression: run Chromatic/visual-diff and confirm no diffs for the icon-only stories
Accessibility: run axe/core checks on button stories and verify aria-busy/labels
Cross-theme check: verify in light/dark/high-contrast and custom theming playground
Mobile: test on iOS/Android webviews for dense toolbars
rollout_plan: 1) Merge PR behind feature flag and enable in internal dev environment. 2) Run visual diffs and internal dogfood apps (console, docs site). 3) Gradual release: enable for 10% of production requests via feature flag controlled in Console, monitor layout-shift metrics. 4) If stable at 48h, increase to 100% and land token migration PRs. 5) Publish migration notes and deprecation timeline for legacy token names.
